statement: On a spring day, the outdoor temperature $T$, in degrees Fahrenheit, $t$ hours after 6:00 a.m. is modeled by $T(t) = -0.5t^2 + 6t + 50$ for $0 \le t \le 12$. According to the model, what is the change in temperature, in degrees Fahrenheit, from 7:00 a.m. to 10:00 a.m.?

choices.misconception: I treated 7:00 a.m. as t = 0 and 10:00 a.m. as t = 3, so I found T(3) - T(0) = 63.5 - 50 = 13.5, but t counts hours after 6:00 a.m.
I found T(4) - T(0) = 66 - 50 = 16, which is the change since 6:00 a.m., but the interval starts at 7:00 a.m., which is t = 1.
I read -0.5t^2 as (-0.5t)^2, which made the squared term positive, so I got T(4) - T(1) = 78 - 56.25 = 21.75.

hints: Turn each clock time into a value of $t$, the number of hours after 6:00 a.m.

solutions.elegant: $T(4) - T(1) = -0.5(16 - 1) + 6(4 - 1) = -7.5 + 18 = 10.5$. The constant $50$ cancels, so it never needs to be added.

author: Devansh Sanghavi
